Second ARIADNA user evaluation to compare brief and explanatory abstention messages, measure understanding and trust and select the clarification format for the v2.2 candidate.

Andrés Beltrán: Twenty research-administration staff are participating. Each will see answerable responses, correct abstentions and controlled errors.
Nuria Castaño: We compare two formats. Format A only states that no reliable answer is available. Format B explains the reason, cites consulted evidence and proposes a clarification where appropriate.
Rosa Mena: For travel questions, format B clearly distinguishes the validity date and language of the rules.
Pablo Herrero: Eighty-six percent of participants correctly identified why the system abstained with format B, compared with 58 percent for format A.
Tomás Leal: Average trust was 4.3 out of 5 with format B and 3.5 with A. However, B messages took longer to read.
Clara Ibáñez: Were the clarifications useful, or did they appear generic?
Pablo Herrero: Eighty-one percent of clarifications were considered useful. The poorest cases added two details at once, such as date and unit.
Nuria Castaño: We can limit each clarification to one dimension and show additional details under an expandable section.
Andrés Beltrán: What happened when the system abstained incorrectly?
Tomás Leal: Participants detected the error more readily when evidence was shown. That reduces false confidence, although it does not eliminate false abstention.
Rosa Mena: For language-unavailable, we should indicate that information may exist in another language without presenting it as an answer in the requested language.
Andrés Beltrán: Format B is selected with a brief main message, expandable evidence and a one-dimension clarification. It will be tested in the v2.2 release candidate.
